High escape phenotype and near-perfect structure compatibility make it a strong replication-safe escape candidate.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to change the final Top-3 because the current rankings are clearly separated by combined escape and structural viability signals.

history.rationale: Known H1 HA antigenic-site position (mature N146); aspartate changes surface charge and commonly appears in antibody-escape variants while likely retaining fitness.
No new evidence yet; retained based on prior plausibility as a HA head antigenic-site mutation with potential escape effect.
Low escape phenotype (0.444) combined with poor structure compatibility (0.258) and near-zero sequence/evolutionary support makes it a weak candidate.

rejection.reason: Low escape phenotype (0.444) combined with poor structure compatibility (0.258) and near-zero sequence/evolutionary support makes it a weak candidate.

history.rationale: Mature K159 in Sb antigenic site; K→N can add an N-glycan (NLT motif) and is a recurrent H1 escape mutation with moderate fitness cost.
No new evidence yet; retained as a surface charge-changing substitution in the HA head.
High escape (0.856) plus excellent structure compatibility (0.925) and moderate MSA frequency (0.207) outweigh the low PLM score; best replication-safe escape candidate.
Mature K170 in Ca1 antigenic site; charge reversal to glutamate should strongly disrupt antibody binding while preserving surface polarity.
No new evidence yet; retained as a charge-reversal mutation likely to alter antibody recognition.
Highest escape (0.877) but moderate structure (0.588) and very low PLM (0.010) increase replication risk; demoted below structurally safer high-escape options.
Mature N129 in Sa antigenic site; Asp substitution alters charge and is plausible for escape without major structural disruption.
No new evidence yet; retained based on location in the HA head and potential antigenic relevance.
High escape (0.863) and relatively best PLM (0.183) but structure N/A and zero MSA frequency create uncertainty; kept but not top-ranked.
Mature Q222 near RBS; Q→R changes size/charge and is a known H1 RBS-adjacent escape-like substitution, though replication impact is possible.
No new evidence yet; retained as a candidate in a potential antigenic region.
High escape (0.770) with strong structure compatibility (0.835) despite low sequence/evolutionary scores; balanced danger candidate.
Mature R225 in RBS; loss of large basic side chain may weaken antibody recognition but could alter receptor binding, so replication is guarded.
No new evidence yet; retained as a possible escape mutation but with lower prior confidence.
Moderate escape (0.599) is not high enough to justify very low PLM (0.000) and moderate structure (0.445).

rejection.reason: Moderate escape (0.599) is not high enough to justify very low PLM (0.000) and moderate structure (0.445).

history.rationale: Mature Y228; conservative aromatic loss of hydroxyl reduces antibody contacts while likely maintaining RBS packing.
No new evidence yet; retained as a conservative aromatic substitution that may alter an epitope.
Excellent structure (0.965) but low escape (0.411) fails the primary objective; not worth retaining.

rejection.reason: Excellent structure (0.965) but low escape (0.411) fails the primary objective; not worth retaining.

history.rationale: Mature R207 in Ca1 antigenic site; glycine removes a surface basic residue and may escape antibodies with limited folding penalty.
No new evidence yet; retained for evaluation against structural and fitness constraints.
Moderate escape (0.682) but strong structure (0.830) keeps it viable; low PLM/MSA limit confidence.
Mature S156 in Sb antigenic site; larger polar side chain may alter epitope surface and is compatible with a surface loop.
No new evidence yet; retained as a potential surface mutation but lower prior confidence.
High escape (0.743) with near-perfect structure (0.912) is a strong replication-safe escape candidate despite low PLM/MSA.
Mature Y144 in antigenic site; histidine changes aromatic/charge character and is a plausible antibody-escape substitution.
No new evidence yet; retained but ranked lower due to possible fitness cost of aromatic-to-histidine change.
Low escape (0.435) and very poor structure compatibility (0.161) make it clearly unsuitable.
